account:
Today I have heard repeated rumours about a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery, involving baker, freight and neighbour. Townsfolk also reported baker carrying bread and wheat, and freight carrying bread at the inn. I did not witness those movements myself, and carrying supplies is not by itself suspicious. Secretary now reports that baker described ordinary freight business and supplied no firsthand evidence of crossing changes; neighbour's crossing story remains unverified. I will have an opportunity to ask neighbour directly at our scheduled fifteen-o'clock tea at the dockside cottage. I do not yet know whether there is any concealed plan, much less what it would accomplish.

My ten-o'clock mill inspection established that the stall held 128 hay bales, equivalent to 1,152 wheat. Neither secretary nor baker has identified the mill keeper, and storage conditions and deliveries remain uninspected. That is an unresolved administrative gap, not evidence of wrongdoing.

Builder reports no visible defects on the bridge and public lighting routes he examined. His inspection was visual, not a full structural survey or nighttime lighting test. He made no purchases or repairs and proposed no charges. He is now asking secretary to record his findings or lend him writing supplies, consistent with my request for a written report.

I am at the town hall for council letters, but secretary has just asked where today's correspondence is kept, so that appointment has not yet produced any letters to review. Overall, there is much repeated hearsay but little verified evidence of anything unusual. My next useful inquiry is to establish what neighbour actually saw or heard, while keeping ordinary town business moving.
